problem: VLA navigation policies such as OmniVLA remain susceptible to perceptual distraction and ambiguous scene interpretation, and no prior work has empirically tested whether visual grounding (overlays, as used for VLMs) helps them.
motivation: Visual prompting with masks or marks improves VLM reasoning, but LLM-based grounding is too slow for real-time navigation and detectors have a fixed vocabulary. The paper asks whether cheap traversability overlays can improve a VLA navigation policy without retraining.
key_idea: Overlay a SegFormer traversable (green) / non-traversable (red) mask on the egocentric observation, and optionally on the goal image or as an appended language instruction, before feeding OmniVLA.
insight: The absolute far-waypoint error reduction largely disappears after normalizing by trajectory length: grounded paths are about 30% shorter (0.63 m vs 0.45/0.43 m), so grounding acts as a length regularizer rather than improving per-distance spatial reasoning. Grounding helps language goals more than image goals (base image error is already 0.13 m), and it cannot fix the out-of-distribution 'stop' instruction, where the model always predicts forward motion.
method: Binary traversability segmentation: SegFormer classifies each pixel of the egocentric RGB image as traversable (floor) or non-traversable (walls, furniture, stairs), running in real time with no fixed object vocabulary.
Observation overlay: the mask is blended onto the image (green = traversable, red = non-traversable) to give the grounded observation i'; the trajectory is tau_1 = VLA(i', g).

Joint grounding (goal augmentation): for image goals the same overlay is applied to the goal image; for language goals the sentence 'keep the trajectory within green traversable areas and avoid red non-traversable areas' is appended; tau_2 = VLA(i', g').
Policy: frozen OmniVLA (omnivla-base and omnivla-finetuned-cast) outputs 7 2D waypoints; no retraining.
Evaluation protocol: open-loop on segments of the Grand Tour ETH-2 indoor episode; error is the minimum Euclidean distance from each predicted waypoint to the ground-truth path, on a Jetson Thor.

setting.backbone: OmniVLA (omnivla-base, omnivla-finetuned-cast; frozen) + SegFormer (binary traversability segmentation)
setting.training_data: none for the grounding (training-free plug-in; no OmniVLA retraining). SegFormer is used as the segmentation module; its training data is not described.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB from an ANYmal D quadruped, with language or goal image
setting.simulator: none (offline replay of the real-robot Grand Tour dataset, episode ETH-2)
setting.privileged: none at inference (ground-truth trajectory used only for evaluation; stair and stop segments manually omitted)

numbers.eval_set_note: single indoor episode ETH-2; 13 short-instruction and 6 long-instruction segments; stair and stop segments omitted
numbers.method: Joint grounding (segmented + augmented), omnivla-base, language goals
numbers.extra: open-loop; metric is error in meters (lower is better); base error 0.095 m overall
numbers.evidence: Table 1 overall average (without stop) 1-7: 0.095 / 0.064 / 0.064; WP7 short 0.187/0.120/0.122, long 0.160/0.090/0.098; text 'average error at the farthest waypoint decreased from 0.22 m (base) to 0.16 m (segmented) and 0.15 m (augmented)'

numbers.eval_set_note: same single episode; observation-only grounding variant
numbers.evidence: Table 1 Segmented column; text: 0.22 m to 0.16 m at farthest waypoint

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark was used (open-loop error on one Grand Tour episode). Some results appear only in figures (per-waypoint curves, path length, image-goal and finetuned-cast overall errors); text ranges were not copied as separate rows.
results: On OmniVLA-base with language goals, grounding reduces far-waypoint (WP7) error from 0.22 m to 0.16 m (segmented) and 0.15 m (augmented), i.e. 27-44% depending on instruction length. Overall average error drops from 0.095 m to 0.064 m. Gains are small for image goals (0.13 m to 0.11-0.12 m), and normalised error is no better than base.
limitations: Evaluation is open-loop and limited to a single indoor episode of one dataset and one VLA (OmniVLA), with no closed-loop task success measured.
The segmentation assumes static 2D traversability, so stairs and dynamic obstacles fail and the stair segments were omitted; the red/green encoding is an untuned heuristic.
Grounding does not fix the 'stop' failure, and the gain is largely an effect of shorter trajectories.
